rubric.evidence: IDL verbatim from xhr.spec.whatwg.org #interface-progressevent; Blink exposure from progress_event.idl at main (base64 from gitiles); ProgressEventInServiceWorker status stable from runtime_enabled_features.json5; CL 8425503 MERGED 2026-10-13 (#1717288) via Gerrit REST; chromiumdash fetch_commit earliest 157.0.8103.0; ServiceWorkerGlobalScope Global=(Worker,ServiceWorker) from the SW spec, Firefox 140 and WebKit-7614 IDL. Every behavioural claim (TypeError on missing type / non-object init / NaN / Infinity, negative accepted, DataCloneError on structuredClone, strict-mode assignment TypeError, XMLHttpRequest still undefined in SW) runtime-verified in headless Chrome 153.0.8010.12, 157.0.8103.78 and 158.0.8127.18.

Feature id 5069584943153152 is in the live milestone=157 listing under 'Enabled by default'; slug derived from the listing name 'Expose ProgressEvent in service workers'; commit first landed in 157.0.8103.0 per Chromium Dash (157 branch point #1717349 > commit #1717288).

reference-contract.json claims implementation-sufficient over 6 inventory items (service-worker exposure, constructor, ProgressEventInit, lengthComputable, loaded, total) x 9 dimensions; attribute getter errors are not-applicable with a spec rationale (getter steps only return the initialized value). The whole IDL is documented locally, so readers do not need MDN.

The page separates what changes (global binding) from what does not (no XHR, no automatic fetch progress events, events not serializable), covers Finch kill-switch semantics and polyfill-collision risk from the ChromeStatus compat notes, and explains the Content-Length vs decoded-bytes mismatch for compressed responses.

The sw.js + page.html download-relay pair was run with the same logic in headless Chrome 153 (fallback path, native=false) and 157.0.8103.78 (native ProgressEvent), 400 kB body, progress+loadend received, 0 page errors (scratch test rt/ex). Constructor and feature-detection snippets are also included, and the showcase scope-probe concept iframe was confirmed to render.

Two tables: (1) SW exposure per browser with evidence and explicit unknowns (Edge unknown, Firefox/Safari first version unknown, Android/WebView from ChromeStatus not device-tested); (2) BCD raw api/ProgressEvent.json interface/member versions. The page notes that BCD worker_support still marks Chrome partial and records engine differences in loaded/total typing (double vs unsigned long long).

Spec anchors confirmed present by grepping the fetched specs (#security-considerations, #suggested-names..., #concept-event-fire-progress, DOM #concept-event-constructor/#dictdef-eventinit/#dispatching-events, SW #serviceworkerglobalscope-interface). Intent links are resolved from ChromeStatus msgid redirects to canonical Google Groups threads. Showcase feature and 3 concept routes returned HTTP 200 on 2026-11-15. All external links use target=_blank rel=noopener.

Single h1; id-anchored h2/h3; captioned tables with thead/scope; scrollable table wraps are keyboard-focusable role=region named via aria-labelledby with a visible focus outline; iframe has a descriptive title; Baseline banner role=note; only CSS variables are used (no raw hex).

Playwright headless Chrome at 1280x800 and 360x740 DPR3 (isMobile+touch): scrollWidth equals clientWidth (1280/360), 0 console errors, 0 failed requests, and the chromestatus link is present. Screenshots read: scratchpad/shots/{desktop,mobile}-{top,examples,compatibility}.png. The SW compat table was adjusted to wrap on mobile after the first screenshot showed the evidence column clipped inside its scroller.

The page embeds the own-feature concept route /v157/expose-progressevent-in-service-workers/scope-probe/ (HTTP 200, carries chromestatus 5069584943153152); the iframe rendered the Global-scope probe at both viewports. Sibling concepts scope-matrix and download-relay are linked. Note: the showcase index says the [Exposed] list was historically (Window,DedicatedWorker,SharedWorker); that describes Blink's IDL, while the spec has always said (Window,Worker). gendn states the spec form.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive browser compatibility data table on narrow mobile without page horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Semantic table with thead/th; wrapper with overflow:auto, tabindex=0, role=region and aria-labelledby the caption; keep cells legible instead of crushing columns.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: compat and init tables wrapped in focusable role=region .table-wrap named by caption ids, thead/scope headers, focus-visible outline. The 3-column SW table wraps at 360px with min-widths on the browser/version columns; the 5-column BCD table keeps min-width 34rem and scrolls inside its region. Exception: no stacked card layout or sticky headers, because the tables are short (6 rows) and the shared house style uses scroll wraps.
